html:
SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown

GUID: a170204d-485c-49a7-b874-ccd99188b760
Slug: unknown-effect
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO started an action but lost contact before it heard back, so it can't tell whether the action happened. The screen shows an error, but the change may still have been made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in this conversation to look at the current state of what the action was changing, without changing anything. This tells you whether the action went through even though the answer was lost.
  2. If SMTO can't reach the Gateway, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection. A dropped connection to the Gateway is the most common reason the answer never arrived.
  3. Only if the check shows the action did not happen, ask SMTO to do it again. Repeating an action that already happened can do the work twice, such as sending something or restarting a service again.

What success looks like

  • The current state shows the change exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the Gateway. Don't repeat the action just because this error appeared; check first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An operation may have begun or taken effect, but SMTO has no trustworthy result for it (for example the Gateway connection dropped or the response was lost after dispatch); a missing acknowledgement is not proof that it failed or never ran.

What this means

  • The operation may have begun, but its final effect is not established by a trustworthy receipt. A lost connection, interrupted adapter or unresolved prior delivery can leave this uncertainty. Repeating the mutation can duplicate work even if the UI shows an error. The current target state and correlated operation receipt must be reconciled first.

Why this can happen

  • Authoritative final confirmation is missing or unusable after possible dispatch. The current resource or operation record is needed to establish what happened.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the existing operation or request ID in the saved receipt. Inspect the affected target with an authorized read and compare its current state with that receipt.
  • If a job is still running, continue observing that same job. If the result cannot be established, leave the operation unresolved rather than issuing a replacement mutation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the affected target with a read-only operation and correlate it with the original operation's receipt before any further mutation. Check Gateway reachability (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check connection). Repeat the mutation only if the read-only check shows it did not take effect.
  • Inspect current state with a read-only operation before performing another mutation. Do not blindly retry the mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Obtain an authoritative current-state observation for the affected target and account for the earlier operation before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The adapter cannot establish final external effects; missing acknowledgment is not proof of failure or nonexecution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
